intent.tagline: One port takes the state. The documents keep the words.
intent.narration: CoBuilder knew what its slices meant and could not say what was next. The ladder lived in a markdown table that any session could contradict. This design gives the state one shared store behind a port, so the tracker can change and the callers stay.

problem_solution.problem: Slice state, scores, and attempts lived in prose tables. Epic branches and pull-request numbers lived in hand-edited joins. Work ran on a local machine, in cloud sessions, and with a team, so the states drifted apart. Nothing answered what is next or what blocks what.
problem_solution.solution: A tracker port sits between CoBuilder and the task system. Beads is the first adapter and the master of programs, epics, slices, and pull requests. The plan proposes a central Dolt-in-git store for the shared backlog. The cloud clone case is not verified. One projector keeps the index the same.
problem_solution.narration: The line is deliberate. Records with a stage, a score, or a position become tracker records. Prose and external facts stay files with pointers. No caller names a tracker.

beats.text: Slice state sits in prose tables, and two sessions on one ladder race at whole-file grain. Local, cloud, and team sessions drift apart.

A TrackerPort carries every read and write of a neutral TrackerRecord, with sync, claim, and pull request operations. Beads is the first adapter. A files adapter, a fake adapter, and one contract test prove the seam.
Agents call one command, shared/tracker.py. One shared reference teaches it, and each skill links it once, so no skill copies a command table.
Program, epic, slice, and pull request become records. A pull request is its own issue and blocks each epic it holds. Gates 1 to 4, Gate 2b, and 4a to 4c are scalar fields on the program.

Every record carries the envelope with kind, version, and the consumer ids the viewer already uses. It holds scalars, paths, and lists of paths. A flat slot, as in Linear, stores a list as a JSON string.
No test yet shows that a clone-only cloud session can run bd init and bd sync against refs/dolt/data. No tracker gives a verified atomic claim. The Linear and Jira rows wait for live accounts.

alternatives.option: Markdown tables as the only state
alternatives.rejected_because: State in prose races at whole-file grain and has no history.

alternatives.option: Beads only, with the bd bridges for Jira and Linear
alternatives.rejected_because: No bridge pushes metadata.cb, so they only mirror.

alternatives.option: Call bd directly, and extract a port later
alternatives.rejected_because: Every caller holds bd calls, and the later extraction rewrites them all.
Network-bound and wrong-grained. ADR-0029 already reads the pull request from GitHub.

architecture.narration: The port sits under the readers and writers. The adapters speak to a tracker, the projector builds the index, and the viewer never learns which tracker runs.

beats.text: The tracker CLI has one subcommand for each port operation. It prints JSON and exits 2 when it has no adapter. A shared reference tells agents when to run each command.
Sessions write state through one command, shared/tracker.py, which calls the port. Every state write needs a configured adapter. With the beads adapter, that means bd.
The port operation sync moves the tracker. On beads it is bd sync, which uses the hidden ref refs/dolt/data in the repo's own git remote. The cloud clone case is not verified.
build_index.py gets TrackerRecord lists from the port, runs the projector, and writes the same index. A later Linear or Jira adapter may cache inside itself.
With no configured adapter, scripts still read the file sources through the files adapter and refuse every state write.
